headline: Navitas and Microchip have released a joint design blueprint that converts 800-volt rack power to 6 volts for AI data centres.
score_reason: Kept at the pool level: a product blueprint with company-set targets and no named customer.
importance_line: Data-centre builders moving to higher-voltage racks, which are meant to distribute power more efficiently, get a ready-made starting design, but the 96% figure is a target set by the companies and no customer or launch date is named.
source: Semiconductor Today, relaying a Navitas and Microchip announcement
summary: Semiconductor Today reports, relaying a joint announcement of 5 Oct 2026, that the US chipmakers Navitas Semiconductor, which makes power chips, and Microchip Technology have built a reference design, a ready-made starting design for other engineers, that converts 800-volt direct current to 6 volts in one step for AI data-centre racks, the cabinets that hold the servers. The companies target up to 96% peak efficiency, a figure they set themselves, and will show the design at the Open Compute Project summit in San Jose on 12 to 15 Oct.
notes: Credit chain: the companies' joint press release (GlobeNewswire, 5 Oct 2026, not reachable here) to Semiconductor Today, the page read. Company targets, not independently tested.
